clue.text: At theatre, professor knocked back liqueur

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the professor and theatre words are read right to left
the professor is put at the theatre, so the professor comes first and the theatre follows

parts.note: a don is a university teacher or professor
rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A professor at the theatre downs a liqueur in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like downing a drink, but it reverses the professor-at-theatre run. 'At' sets the order: professor first, then theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured spirit, a brand of liqueur.

clue.text: She's knocked over beer around bridge opponents

indicators.note: around means the reversed beer goes round the bridge players
something knocked over is upended, so the beer word is turned back to front

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
in bridge East and North sit as opponents, giving E and N

explanation.surface: A woman has tipped over a beer during a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' reverses the beer to ELA, which goes 'around' the bridge players. In bridge, North and East sit next to each other on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Elena is a woman's name, so a female pronoun stands for it in crossword fashion.

parts.note: neck is slang for cheek or impudence
a tie is a match or game in sport

explanation.surface: Someone has the cheek to wear matching clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is an item of clothing worn round the collar.

indicators.note: the first two letters of the last word are read as in, putting the organ inside the rest of the word

parts.note: taken as written
the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: An exclamation that an organ was indeed rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'indeed' as emphasis, but split it as 'in deed' to get the container and its outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be delivered is to be rescued or saved, as in delivered from evil.

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a hearse is the car you ride in once you are the late, deceased

explanation.surface: A driver practises in the car when running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead here, not behind time.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to go through something for practice before performing it.

indicators.note: pirates imprison means the word pirates holds the answer locked inside its letters

explanation.surface: Pirates lock up a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for a traitor or informer who betrays others.

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for causing pain is taken as spoken

parts.note: hurts means causes pain

explanation.surface: A physicist inflicts pain, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Hertz was a German physicist who proved electromagnetic waves exist.

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for an ensign, the officer carrying a flag, as Iago is called in Othello

explanation.surface: An elderly flag carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, and was also the Elizabethan term for an ensign carrying the colours.

clue.text: Oarsman in trouble in the smallest republic

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things in disarray, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rower gets into difficulty in a tiny country.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is often called the world's smallest republic, an enclave in Italy.

clue.text: Each high spot should contain a soft-drink filter machine

indicators.note: should contain means the soft drink goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: per means each, as in so much per head
a tor is a rocky hill or high point
cola is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: Every high viewpoint ought to have a soft-drink filter.
explanation.definitionFit: A percolator is a coffee maker that filters boiling water through grounds.

clue.text: Stick is able to break in the middle

parts.note: can means is able

indicators.note: in the middle picks out the centre letter of break

explanation.surface: A stick that can snap in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane is a walking stick or rod.

parts.note: aft means at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A foolish girl sits at the back of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is a British informal synonym for foolish.

clue.text: The French come to university with style, for South American

parts.note: venez is the French for come
elan means flair or style

explanation.surface: A French person comes to university with flair, for a Latin American course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French come' wants LE plus a word for come; it is the French word for come itself, VENEZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venezuelan is a person from Venezuela, in South America.

indicators.note: run here means set going in a new way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: I manage a casino in Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, so it lies there.

definitions.meaning: a lifelong occupation or line of work

explanation.surface: A rush toward getting a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Career means both to rush along wildly and a person's working life.

clue.text: Blast area destroyed to find gypsum

indicators.note: destroyed suggests the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A demolition zone reveals a soft mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine-grained form of the mineral gypsum used for carving.

clue.text: Drink from a tap at the back

parts.note: a cock is a tap or valve, as in stopcock
the tail is the back end

explanation.surface: Someone pours a drink from a tap at the rear of the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a mixed alcoholic drink.

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone able to lure people once they are away.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent means capable or able to do something well.

parts.note: reads like someone undressing for money, but means printed stripes that encode a price at the till

explanation.definitionFit: Barcodes are patterns of printed stripes scanned to read a product's price.

clue.text: One applauds part of the "Ring Cycle"?

definitions.meaning: the striker inside a bell that makes it ring, with a nod to Wagner's opera cycle

explanation.surface: An audience member clapping at Wagner's Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapper is both a person clapping and the tongue that strikes a bell.

definitions.meaning: the town ... Keynes in Buckinghamshire has this word before the surname of the economist John Maynard Keynes

explanation.surface: A poet ahead of an economist in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county, home of the new town Milton Keynes.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton the poet shares his name with the first half of Milton Keynes.

clue.text: Supply of reading material for stars on railway

parts.note: Libra is a constellation of stars

explanation.surface: Reading matter for celebrities travelling by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a collection of books held for people to borrow and read.

clue.text: Analyse a harp arrangement in this free rendering

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters within the word for analyse

parts.note: to parse is to analyse grammatically

indicators.note: an arrangement is a reordering, so the letters of a harp are reset

explanation.surface: A musician analyses a harp arrangement, in a loose interpretation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' turns A HARP into APHRA, which goes 'in' PARSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase restates something loosely in other words.

definitions.meaning: to rise and fall like the sea

explanation.surface: Feeling queasy on a rolling sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Heave means both to rise with a swell and to retch.

clue.text: Great deal of money for a worn-out car

definitions.meaning: as in it cost a fortune
slang for an old dilapidated vehicle

explanation.surface: Paying a fortune for an old banger.
explanation.definitionFit: Bomb is British slang both for a large sum and, in Australia, for an old wreck of a car.

parts.note: ma is mum, with the 's meaning is
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Mother disapproves of drinking wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Macon is a French wine from the Burgundy region.

clue.text: Stage a bit of a dance

definitions.meaning: a single movement of the feet in dancing

explanation.surface: Performing part of a dance on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is both a stage in progress and one movement in a dance routine.

clue.text: Perhaps crab gall is a meat accompaniment

parts.note: a crab apple is a kind of the fruit, so crab is an example
sauce means cheek or impudence, as does gall

explanation.surface: A crab with nerve is served alongside meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crab' is not the shellfish but the crab apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple sauce is a classic condiment served with roast pork.

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A father makes time for his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat is a girl's name, short for Patricia.

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters behave badly and go astray

explanation.surface: A saucy act at the end of the pier.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient means having an excessive interest in sexual matters, much like lewd.

clue.text: Working in a court can be distressing

definitions.meaning: hearing a case as a judge

explanation.surface: Court work can be upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying means both hearing a case in court and being hard to endure.
